The mass of a radioactive tracer in a sample is initially $24$ milligrams and decreases with time, as shown in the graph. Which of the following is closest to the time, in hours, from the initial measurement at which the mass of the tracer is $40%$ of its initial value?
explanation: Choice C is correct. The graph shows that the mass starts at $24$ milligrams and follows an exponential decay pattern. First, $40\%$ of the initial value is $0.40 \times 24 = 9.6$ milligrams. From the graph, the mass reaches approximately $9.6$ milligrams at about $t = 1.3$ hours. This can also be verified using the exponential model $M(t) = 24(0.5)^{t}$: setting $24(0.5)^{t} = 9.6$ gives $(0.5)^{t} = 0.40$, so $t = \frac{\ln(0.40)}{\ln(0.5)} \approx 1.32$. Among the given choices, $1.32$ is closest to this value.
